rows.11:4bb4:
I see.
What a coincidence.
The story I've prepared happens to be about a ghost.
{a}, the truth is...
This is a ghost story, but it's also my confession.
Please, hear it through to the end.
...Well then, let me tell it.
You see, there's something else that appears in that lodge besides ghosts.
I'll tell you what it is.{p}
rows.11:508c:
...That's right, inside the lodge.
Believe it or not, he'd been in the soccer club, the same as me.
Well, he'd already graduated by the time I joined, so I never met him.
Anyway, about this Reaper Pencil.
They say that if you use it, you can do automatic writing.
The pencil's power moves your hand on its own, and it writes out a certain message.
Now, about that message.
Apparently it reveals what the person using the Reaper Pencil will do that will get them killed.
For example, 'running out into the road,' or 'getting into a fight with someone'...
They say it's a pencil that can predict that kind of thing.
What I'm going to tell you is something that happened involving this Reaper Pencil.
It was last summer.
During the soccer club's training camp, a boy found the Reaper Pencil.
His name was Michio Yamamoto.{p}
rows.11:58c0:
Under his bed, of all things, there was a girl.
"W-who are you?"
Yamamoto was startled, and his face went red.
Then the girl said this.
"I ran away from home..."
The girl was wearing this school's uniform.
She said that she'd run away from home and had come here meaning to stay in the school's lodge.
And so Yamamoto got a bed ready for her, and she slept in the lodge.{p}
rows.11:66b4:
She was apparently a girl who had died three years earlier.
She had run away from home in the very same season as Yamamoto's training camp, and stayed in the school's lodge all by herself.
And after spending day after day alone at the school, she must have grown dark and depressed.
Or perhaps the spirits that stir in this school were working on her.
She jumped from a window of the lodge...
After her suicide, her ghost would often appear in that lodge.
But now that Yamamoto has gone to the same world as her, I suppose she isn't lonely anymore.
Her ghost doesn't appear anymore.
Yamamoto, though, still seems to have lingering attachments to this world.
Ever since then, he's said to appear inside the lodge from time to time.
And after Yamamoto appears, her voice echoes all around...
And Yamamoto's ghost fades away in an instant, as if summoned by her voice, they say.
I couldn't do anything for Yamamoto.
That's why I quit the soccer club.
I was too afraid to face Yamamoto's ghost in the lodge...
That's the kind of man I am.
The lowest kind of man there is...
Well then, let me hand things over to the next person.
I've told you the truth.
So please, all of you, confess everything as well.
Now, whose turn is next...?{p}
rows.11:6b0c:
I see.
Then I suppose I have no choice but to tell this story.
In that lodge... the Upside-Down Woman appears.
She's a monster who peers down at people sleeping in their beds.
Hanging head-down with her long hair dangling, she asks the person sleeping in the bed a certain question.
What kind of question, you ask?
That... I'll get to in due course.
It was last summer.
The soccer club I'd joined used that lodge for its training camps.
Actually, I joined the soccer club because a good friend of mine invited me.
Not that I had any thought of building up my body through sports or anything.
I just got interested from listening to my friend talk about it, that's all.{p}
rows.11:6eb8:
It was a hot, muggy night.
The lodge had no air conditioning and no window screens, so mosquitoes were flying all around in the heat; conditions couldn't have been worse.
And we had to lay our exhausted bodies down on those hard beds.
It was just miserable.
Even in the middle of the night, I couldn't get to sleep.
And then...{p}
rows.11:7a78:
After that, I looked into the Upside-Down Woman.
The record was on the wall down low, beneath one of the beds in the lodge.
It must have been written long ago by someone who had run into the Upside-Down Woman.
A horrifying fact was written there.{p}
rows.11:7b50:
The Upside-Down Woman was a murderous monster.
First, she tries to make a promise with her prey.
The promise can be anything, but apparently it's usually to keep a secret.
And then, later, she comes to kill whoever breaks the promise.
It's a terrifying story.
There's no telling which bed in the lodge the Upside-Down Woman will appear at.
So you can't let your guard down.
When you're using that facility.
There's only one way to avoid being killed by the Upside-Down Woman.
You must never make a promise with her.
If you never make a promise, you can't break a promise to her, after all.
Or else, never break the promise.
But I think it's extremely hard to avoid breaking a promise to her.
She uses every trick there is to make her prey break the promise.
She doesn't kill anyone except those who've broken a promise.
She can't kill anyone else.
Why, you ask?
Without a reason to justify it, she can't commit murder.
Whether breaking a promise counts as a reason for murder... I do have my doubts.
But she's a monster who has always held fast to one motto: promise-breakers die.
There are all sorts of rumors about this, but apparently the Upside-Down Woman became what she is because of something she witnessed right after she was born.
What happened was this: the Upside-Down Woman's mother, a monster, killed her father, another monster.
The mother monster insisted that she had killed the father monster because he broke a promise, so he was the one in the wrong.
And so the idea that promise-breakers must be killed took root in the Upside-Down Woman's heart.
Sodeyama was killed because he broke his promise to the Upside-Down Woman.
...Do you see what that means?
The Upside-Down Woman made Sodeyama promise not to tell anyone about her.
"Try telling someone you trust that you met me."
She said that too, but that was only advice.
It wasn't a promise.
Sodeyama was tricked.
He fell into her trap and broke his promise not to tell anyone.
{a}.
This is why I quit the soccer club.
I can't forget Sodeyama, hacked to pieces right in front of me.
I couldn't stay in a soccer club that held such awful memories.
{a}.
If you ever stay at that lodge, you'd better be careful too.
Listen, you must never, ever make a promise with the Upside-Down Woman.
Otherwise...
You'll meet the same fate as Sodeyama...
That's the end of my story.
Now then, next person, please...{p}
rows.11:87c4:
I see.
So that's the kind of story you like.
The story I'm about to tell is meant for someone exactly like you.
First, before I tell you about the thing I mentioned that appears in the lodge, there's something I need to tell you.
Listen carefully.
It's about the habits of insects.
You know... when people keep or catch bugs, they use a bug cage, right?
And bugs that get shoved into a bug cage want to get out, don't they?
When that happens, some bugs try to push their heads through the bars of the cage.
A bug like that can't get its body out through the bars, so it tries to pull back into the cage the head it went to all that trouble to get out.
And then...
Sometimes it can't pull it back in properly, it catches on the bars, and the bug's head comes right off.
The head that came off rolls outside the bars, and inside the cage lies a headless bug carcass.{p}
rows.11:933c:
And where he ended up was inside that lodge...
The next day, Ono was lying collapsed in the lodge, with his head stuck out through the rails of a bed.
rows.11:96dc:
I saw it too.
During the soccer club's training camp.
It had a truly terrifying look on its face.
I thought that if that face kept looking at me, I'd be cursed.
That's how full of hatred that head's face was.
I slipped out of camp and went home.
That day, one of the seniors called me and told me to hurry back to camp.
But I was too scared to go back.
So I decided to quit the club.
Things had gotten awkward between me and the seniors and the others in my year...
What?
Which bed in the lodge is it, you ask?
...If you want to know, you'll have to check for yourself.
Why not go there and see?
Ono's head really is beautiful, you know...
That's the end of my story.
Whose turn is it next...?{p}
rows.11:9c70:
"What am I going to do with this kitten?"
With nowhere in particular to go, Takeda headed to the school, holding the kitten.
"Isn't there somewhere I could keep it?"
And then she remembered that there was a lodge above the auditorium.{p}
rows.11:8ae8:
...Oh, what's the matter, {a}?
You like disgusting stories, don't you?
You look pale.{p}Could it be you want to stop already?
